entry.title: Connection Escrow: Holding AI-Agent Pod Egress in the Kernel Until an Isolated Verifier Rules
entry.summary:
AI agents in containers act by opening network connections, and the text that drives them can be hostile. Controls placed between the agent and its tools are bypassed by a child process or a direct socket, and their approval is not tied to the connection the kernel later opens. We present connection escrow: every outbound TCP connection from a supervised pod is parked inside the kernel's connect() path, before any packet exists, by a 98-instruction eBPF program on the pod's cgroup.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #networking

entry.title: One year later: the power of 1.1.1.1 interns
entry.summary:
A year after announcing our goal to hire 1,111 interns, more than 750 early-career builders have shipped real products across 48 teams at Cloudflare. From Birthday Week launches to post-quantum security, our interns prove that AI amplifies human potential instead of replacing it.

Source: Cloudflare Systems & Network Engineering · Tags: #networking #performance #post-quantum

entry.title: K-AoI: A Spatio-Temporal Synchronization Metric for Digital Twin-based Teleoperation in Dynamic Network Environments
entry.summary:
Synchronization between a digital twin (DT) and its physical robot is critical for effective teleoperation, as mismatches directly degrade operator awareness and task performance. Existing synchronization metrics are predominantly time-based and rarely capture the spatial consequences of delayed information during motion. In this paper, we introduce Kinematic Age of Information (K-AoI), a spatio-temporal metric that weights AoI by instantaneous Cartesian velocity, translating temporal staleness into physically meaningful spatial divergence.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #robotics #networking
